title: Stretch: Sophisticated Transactional Writing Adventure
welcome_lead: Push your transactional writing to top-band levels — control, nuance, voice.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language stretch — sophisticated transactional writing, rhetorical control, voice.
final_note: You explored advanced rhetorical control — irony, voice, conceptual structures and sustained tone.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Pick a controlling image — say, a sinking ship — and weave it through your whole article.

It gives writing intellectual unity.

Praise the very thing you're attacking: 'What a wonderful idea to fine the homeless for sleeping outside.'

Top markers reward controlled, signalled irony.

Echo earlier images. Use semantic chains. Repeat a key noun with variation.

True cohesion isn't just 'however' and 'furthermore' — it's a web of ideas.

A syntactic unit headed by a noun, which may include determiners, adjectives and modifiers — e.g. 'the big red car' is a noun phrase functioning as a single grammatical unit.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a phoneme and a grapheme?
options: Phonemes are vowels and graphemes are consonants.
A phoneme is the smallest unit of sound in a language; a grapheme is the written letter or letters that represent it.
Phonemes are letters and graphemes are syllables.
